subtopic: Being idolised or hated by juniors
passage:
The design studio was quiet after six when Yamini noticed Vaibhav rehearsing her habit of ending every client call with "let's keep it light." A second junior, wearing the same tote bag as Yamini, did the same the next morning. Even the way she tapped her pen on the table had spread.

She waited until the Friday review, then said to the four juniors, "You can borrow how I organise files. Please don't borrow how I skip lunch, or my habit of promising deadlines I miss. Those are flaws, not style."

Vaibhav laughed, a little startled. "We thought that was how you stay so calm."

"I'm not calm," Yamini said. "I'm behind. Ask me when I'm behind." Someone slid a sandwich across the table, and she took it.

qa.q: Which habit of Yamini's did Vaibhav rehearse after six o'clock?
qa.a: Vaibhav rehearsed her habit of ending every client call with "let's keep it light."

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling as she noticed her habits spreading?
qa.a: She felt uneasy under the weight of being a model, and naming her flaws aloud shows she wanted the juniors to see the real her, not a perfect one.

qa.q: What could Yamini do to keep being an honest model over time?
qa.a: She could keep admitting when she is behind and show the juniors how she recovers, for example by resetting a deadline openly instead of hiding it.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav have seen Yamini's calm before Friday?
qa.a: Vaibhav thought her calm was a skill worth copying, so hearing that she was actually behind probably changed the picture of what to imitate.

grounding: Juniors copy Yamini's style and flaws; she admits imperfection and asks them to copy the useful parts only.

passage:
At the Excel Coaching Centre above the cloth shop in Sehore, Irfan sir had a way of snapping his marker cap shut when a student gave a wrong answer. He also said "Simple, na?" after every problem.
One Tuesday he sat at the back of Yash's trial class. Yash, three months into the job, stood like Irfan, joked like Irfan, said "Simple, na?" and, when a girl in the second row got a sum wrong, snapped his marker cap shut. The girl shrank in her seat.
Irfan felt his stomach drop. That was his own habit, played back to him.
After class he told Yash, "The jokes are fine. The cap thing, don't copy that. I do it when I'm impatient, and it makes kids scared to try. I'm working on stopping."
Yash looked surprised. "You do that?"
"Every day. You didn't notice?"

qa.q: What did Irfan say after every problem?
What was Irfan feeling as he watched Yash snap the marker cap shut?
qa.a: He felt uneasy and a little ashamed, his stomach dropping at seeing his own impatient habit copied and hurting a student.

qa.q: What did Irfan do about being copied?
qa.a: He told Yash which habit not to copy, admitted it was his own flaw from impatience, and said he was working on stopping.

qa.q: How might the girl in the second row experience the snapped cap?
qa.a: She likely felt embarrassed and scared to try again, shrinking in her seat after the wrong answer.

grounding: Juniors copy the protagonist's style and flaws; he feels the weight of being a model, admits the flaw honestly, and becomes more careful.

subtopic: Being idolised or hated by juniors
passage:
In the Lisbon café where Noa had worked for three years, the new baristas had started saying "beautiful, beautiful" when they finished a milk pour, just like her. Priscila even tied her apron the same odd way.
It was sweet, until Saturday. A customer asked for oat milk and Priscila sighed loudly, rolling her eyes, before making it. Noa went cold. She had done exactly that last month, on a bad day, and thought no one noticed.
At closing she found Priscila wiping the steam wand. "Can I tell you something embarrassing? That sigh at the oat-milk guy, I think you got it from me. It was rude when I did it, too."
Priscila blinked. "I thought that was just how you handle annoying orders."
"It's how I handle them badly. I'm trying to do better. You can watch that part too."

qa.q: What did the new baristas say when they finished a milk pour?
What did Noa feel when she saw Priscila sigh at the customer?
qa.a: She felt a cold jolt of embarrassment and responsibility, recognising her own rude habit from a bad day being copied.

qa.q: What made Noa's response to Priscila honest and helpful?
qa.a: She admitted the flaw was hers, called it rude, and said she was working to do better, instead of pretending to be perfect.

qa.q: How might Priscila see Noa after this talk?
qa.a: Priscila may be surprised, then relieved to learn that the person she copies has flaws too and is willing to admit them.

grounding: Juniors copy the protagonist's style and even her flaws; she feels the weight of being a model and admits her imperfection honestly.
